svg.text: Air-brake lag (added) -- 1/2 second or more -- 32 ft

text.font-family: Liberation Sans, DejaVu Sans, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif
text.tspan: Empty trucks often take longer to stop than loaded ones (less traction on the drive axles).
Speed doubles? Braking distance roughly quadruples. Wet or downhill roads add still more distance.
Brake lag is the time air takes to travel through the lines after you push the pedal -- about 1/2 second or more,
roughly 32 more feet at 55 mph. That is why air-brake totals are over 450 feet in this handbook example.
Keep enough space so you can stop. Following-distance seconds are in Figure GK-2.
